summary_alerts.html:
CONSENSUS BUY — META (3 members: Khanna D + McCaul R + Fields D, cross-party)
Meta Platforms was independently bought by all three of the dataset’s most active traders — a Democrat from Silicon Valley, a Republican from Texas, and a Democrat from Louisiana. Fields accumulated ~$250K across two dates; McCaul added 2 positions; Khanna also bought in. Three-member cross-party agreement is the single strongest signal in this dataset.

CONVICTION REACCUMULATION — GS (McCormick: sold $3M in Jan, bought back 7× since Feb)
McCormick — former Goldman Sachs CEO — sold $3M of GS on Jan 23 at $918.88, then turned around and bought back $1.225M across 7 separate purchases from Feb 23 through Mar 10. This is a textbook high-conviction reaccumulation: take profits at the high, then reload at lower prices. No one in this dataset has deeper institutional knowledge of Goldman than McCormick.

CONSENSUS BUY — NFLX (McCaul R 4× + Fields D, cross-party)
Netflix was bought 4 times by McCaul and once by Fields — independent cross-party accumulation. McCaul’s repeated purchasing across multiple dates signals sustained conviction rather than a one-off entry.

CONSENSUS BUY — PEAK / ADSK / ABT (Khanna D + McCaul R, cross-party)
Three additional cross-party pairs: Healthpeak Properties (PEAK, with McCaul buying a large $175K position), Autodesk (ADSK, Khanna 2× + McCaul), and Abbott Laboratories (ABT, both members ~$32K each). Multiple independent bipartisan buy signals in the same window reinforce the broader bullish posture of this group.

CONSENSUS SELL — INTU (3 members: Khanna D + McCaul R + Gottheimer D, cross-party)
Intuit was sold by three members including cross-party agreement between Khanna and McCaul. This is the broadest sell signal in the dataset. Notably, McCaul also bought INTU 3× earlier in the window — suggesting he rotated out of a position he had been building, which adds weight to the exit.

CONSENSUS SELL — UBER (3 members: Khanna D + McCaul R 2× + Gottheimer D, cross-party)
Uber was sold by three members across both parties. Gottheimer, Khanna, and McCaul all exited independently. Three-member cross-party consensus sell is a strong bearish signal.

CONSENSUS SELL — AMZN & HUM (Khanna D + McCaul R, cross-party)
Amazon was sold by both Khanna and McCaul (McCaul 2×). Humana (HUM) was also sold cross-party — McCaul exited a $75K position and Khanna also sold. Health insurer exits may reflect regulatory or policy headwinds anticipated by members with relevant committee exposure.

Observation

Khanna is the highest-volume trader in the group with 266 public equity trades. His clearest conviction plays are ACI (Albertsons, 8×) and Gartner/IT (7×) — repeated accumulation that suggests deliberate position building rather than passive allocation. His largest sector allocation is financials (~$1.12M in buys: BRK/B, MA, BLK, COIN), surprising for the Silicon Valley representative but reflecting a macro bet on financial infrastructure. His exits cluster in tech software and platform names — AXTA (5× sells), GOOGL, UBER, AMZN, PANW — suggesting a rotation from high-multiple growth into value and financial infrastructure.

McCaul is a balanced trader — exactly 58 buys and 58 sells, with net sell volume slightly exceeding buy volume (~$1.81M out vs. ~$1.52M in). His largest single buy is FCN (FTI Consulting, 3× ~$240K), suggesting a consulting/restructuring sector thesis. As Chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, his exits from European industrial names (ASML, BAYRY) and his accumulation of SAP (6×) may reflect views on US-Europe trade dynamics.

Observation

McCormick’s portfolio is entirely concentrated in Goldman Sachs — the firm he formerly ran as CEO. He sold $3M at $918.88 on Jan 23 (near the 52-week high), then systematically bought back $175K/trade across 7 transactions from Feb 23 through Mar 10. The net effect is he locked in ~$1.775M in gains and is now rebuilding the position at lower prices. This is exactly the kind of informed, disciplined trading you’d expect from someone with deep structural knowledge of the firm. The most high-conviction single-name trade in this dataset.

Moore is the fastest filer in the group (~11-day lag), making his data the most current and actionable. His portfolio thesis is distinctly Main Street consumer: LGIH (entry-level homebuilder, 4× ~$172K), HOG (Harley-Davidson, 2× ~$65K), CBRL (Cracker Barrel). As a North Carolina representative, his homebuilder conviction in LGIH is likely informed by on-the-ground awareness of regional housing demand. His telecom rotation — selling VZ and partially selling T while buying T — suggests a preference for AT&T’s fiber buildout story over Verizon.

Fields is the purest bull in the group — 100% buys, zero sells. She made three concentrated cluster purchases: on Jan 20 (Inauguration Day: META $75K, IREN $75K, NFLX $75K), on Feb 3 (GOOGL $175K, META $175K, MU $175K, AMD $75K — ~$600K deployed in a single session), and on Mar 12 (MSFT 2×). The Feb 3 cluster is the most notable event: four coordinated AI-semiconductor buys on one day at prices that now look prescient. Her GOOGL position (~$358K across 3 dates) is the single largest individual name exposure in the entire dataset.
